content_html:
Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens on your PC, from your own copy of the game.

Important

This repository does not contain the game, keys or an executable, and it does not explain how to get them. You need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files.

Discord: https://discord.gg/rexed

Project status

Early. The game does not boot yet. Everything that can be done without the game's executable is in place, so work on booting can start as soon as one is available to a developer.

What Status

Texture dictionaries and world texture pools (DDS) ✅ Exported. Music/radio config ? Measured. 1,589 audio-config records with exact durations and AWC stream ids; station grouping and content-id lists; no per-track start offsets (notes)
PE loader and import shims ⚠️ Runs a stand-in executable end to end (gta6rt --run: CRT startup, statics, heap, files, threads, GDK imports through the shims, exit code back). Untested against the real executable
Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan ⚠️ In progress. A Vulkan-backed device behind the Xbox-ABI proxy creates queues, command lists, fences, descriptor heaps, committed and reserved resources, render-target and depth views (3D targets included), texture views and samplers (2D, cube and 3D views, the depth and stencil planes of depth-stencil textures, packed formats such as B5G6R5, B4G4R4A4 and R9G9B9E5; they go into the bindless set), and query heaps. Barriers, clears, uploads, copies (BC included), colour resolves, predication, CPU-side texture reads and writes, and occlusion, timestamp and pipeline-statistics queries run on Vulkan, checked on one GPU. No buffer views, root signatures, pipelines, draws, placed resources, 1D textures or swapchain yet (plan)
Ray tracing (BVH) ⚠️ In progress. BuildRaytracingAccelerationStructure builds BLASes and TLASes on the GPU in the console's XDXR BVH4 layout (the default; LEONIDA_RT_AS=khr uses Vulkan's own acceleration structures instead), which the translated shaders walk themselves through image_bvh_intersect_ray (all four triangle node types, TRI0-TRI3, with the barycentric remap byte); the GPU builder writes TRI0 leaves. Updates refit instead of rebuilding, and clone, compaction and the compacted/current postbuild sizes work; checked against a CPU reference on synthetic scenes. The build descriptions are recovered from the package's XboxBvhBuilder.dll (notes). The game's *_bvh4.rpf packs are measured: offline-built, dehydrated BLASes that rehydrate through that DLL with their geometry from the drawables in levels.rpf (measured on 8 of the 10 sampled BLAS; notes). Not done in the builder: TRI1 pairing, BOX16 nodes, serialization. Open: whether the game rehydrates the packs or rebuilds them (#313)

The table above is written by hand. To measure it on your own checkout (unit and runtime tests, which rows of the translator contract were confirmed on a GPU, measured imports, your corpus counts and, with --github, CI and the D3D- items), run python -I tools/progress_dashboard.py --out <folder outside the repo> and open progress.html (notes).

Platforms

Nothing is playable on any platform yet (see Project status). What runs where today:

Platform Today
Windows Everything: make_game.py, the tools, and the runtime (gta6rt and the D3D12 → Vulkan layer) with its tests.
Linux The translator, the asset tools and the Vulkan GPU test tools build and run natively (tested on RADV and NVIDIA). The runtime is Windows code: it cross-compiles with clang-cl and xwin, and its tests run under Wine or Proton (The Windows runtime on Linux, under Wine or Proton below). The game is meant to run the same way, under Wine or Proton with the D3D12 layer on native Vulkan (#217).
macOS (Apple Silicon) The Python tools and the Vulkan test tools run natively, on MoltenVK (Homebrew) or KosmicKrisp. The runtime is Windows code and runs as on Linux, under Wine: CrossOver, arm64 with FEX or x86-64 under Rosetta (#1706, #1707, #1924; #3119 fixes the last loader tests there). Known gaps: no geometry stage and no VK_EXT_mesh_shader (those tests are skipped), 32-wide subgroups (wave64 shaders run emulated), and MoltenVK's float handling (PerVertexKHR, NaN compares, -0, the cost of NoContraction); docs/testing.md lists each (#2947).
AMD RDNA1 (RX 5000) A supported target: close to the console's RDNA2, and its 64-wide subgroups run the wave64 shaders natively. RX 5700 XT results pass the GPU test suite (#146); on RADV, pixel shaders without fragment barycentrics have a known difference (Known problems in docs/testing.md) (#330).

GPU results from every platform are collected in #166; how to run the tests is in docs/testing.md.

How to build

The port isn't downloaded ready-made. It's built on your PC from your own copy.

The easy way:

  1. Install the prerequisites below.
  2. Download this project with its submodule: git clone --recursive https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out third_party/rpf9-explorer. The build fetches it if git is installed, and otherwise tells you what to do.
  3. Double-click Build.bat.

It finds your copy of the game by itself: it looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents (also where Windows keeps them, such as in OneDrive), Games, your home folder and the top of every drive, two folders deep. It recognises the version from a few file sizes, without reading anything large. If you have more than one copy it asks which one, and if it finds none it asks you to paste the folder. Before starting it checks that everything below is installed and that there is enough free space, and it lists anything missing in one go. The result goes to Documents\Leonida. A stopped build continues where it left off.

Your game folder is the one that holds MicrosoftGame.Config and the .rpf archives, as plain files.

Prerequisites:

  • Your own copy of the Xbox Series package, version 1.0.2.1.
  • Windows 10/11 x64, with about 350 GB free for work files. They can go on another drive with --work.
  • Python 3.12+ (tick "Add python.exe to PATH").
  • .NET 8 SDK.
  • Vulkan SDK, for spirv-as / spirv-val.
  • LLVM 21+ with the AMDGPU target for llvm-mc. The official Windows build has no AMDGPU target. On Windows, scripts\build_llvm_mc.ps1 builds a native llvm-mc.exe with it (no WSL; needs git and the Visual Studio C++ tools below) and sets LLVM_MC; it takes about 20-40 minutes. A faster way, if you use conda: conda install -c conda-forge llvm-tools (its Windows build includes the AMDGPU target; docs/testing.md used version 23.1.6), then set LLVM_MC to the full path of the llvm-mc.exe it installs (where llvm-mc shows it once the environment is active). Or install llvm-21 in WSL and set LLVM_MC to the whole command, LLVM_MC="wsl -d Ubuntu -e /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc" (see docs/design.md). On Linux, llvm-mc on PATH is enough.
  • Visual Studio 2022 with Desktop development with C++ and the Windows SDK 10.0.26100 or newer, for the runtime stage (the runtime uses version 1.2 root signatures, which older SDKs don't declare).
  • ffmpeg on PATH (optional: decodes the XMA2 streams, and required for --wav).

Low disk space: the ~350 GB figure is for the full build. To run the port, --stages check,shaders,runtime needs about 30 GB; the assets stage (~300 GB) is only for the asset tools, and --wav adds several times the Ogg Opus size (the preflight prints this choice when the assets stage is what does not fit). --work and --out can sit on another drive. The runtime maps the package in place, so a read-only package drive needs gta6rt --overlay <writable folder>; --overlay is a gta6rt option, not a make_game.py one. Leave the .s files in work/shaders/dxbc/disasm in place: deleting them, along with the translated work/shaders/spirv/index.json, can leave the shaders stage looking finished with zero shaders. A disasm folder that is a symlink is refused when the stage has to clear it.

From a terminal, with the same behaviour and more control:

python -I make_game.py --find                          # list the copies found on this PC
python -I make_game.py --pick                          # choose the game folder in a folder dialog
python -I make_game.py --check                         # check your copy, build nothing
python -I make_game.py --check --full-check            # also compare SHA-256 of every file (slow)
python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --out "D:\Games\Leonida" --work "E:\leonida-work"
python -I make_game.py --stages shaders,assets         # only some stages
python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --wav   # also decode Opus to PCM WAV (large)
python -I make_game.py --wave64-emulate off            # auto (default), on or off; see below

--wave64-emulate decides whether wave64 compute and mesh shaders are translated to be exact on any subgroup size (see "Wave64 emulation" in docs/design.md). NVIDIA and Intel GPUs have 32-wide subgroups and need it. The default, auto, asks vulkaninfo (part of the Vulkan SDK) and turns emulation on if any GPU lacks 64-wide subgroups or its subgroup size is unknown. It also checks whether the runtime's GPU can run compute and mesh shaders 64-wide. With --mesh-compute, only compute subgroup support is needed.

On AMD's Windows driver, auto uses native wave64 on RDNA1 and RDNA2 when the runtime's GPU supports it, even if another GPU is 32-wide or vulkaninfo is unavailable. That driver can crash on emulated LDS code (#857). For RDNA1 cards without mesh support, the decision uses the compute stage, which can run wave64 without native mesh support.

The mode is saved next to the translated shaders, and changing it translates them again. auto can normally reuse previously emulated shaders. The AMD Windows workaround rebuilds those shaders in native mode. Use --wave64-emulate on to force emulation or --wave64-emulate off to force native wave64.

Four fallback flags are forwarded to the translator the same way, saved next to the translated shaders, and changing them translates them again: --no-float-controls (drop SignedZeroInfNanPreserve, for devices whose pipeline check skips a shader without shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32; needs PR #664's translator flag), --bary-fallback (read raw barycentrics from an interpolated input, for devices without VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric), --texel-offset-fallback (fold image_sample*_o offsets into the coordinate, for devices without VK_KHR_maintenance8) and --mesh-compute (mesh shaders as compute, for devices without VK_EXT_mesh_shader). Each is documented in docs/design.md.

The build records which llvm-mc command and version produced the disassembly. Changing either, or reusing a work folder that predates this record, reruns disassembly and translation while keeping the extracted shader inputs.

The build records which translator sources produced the shaders. A change to those files reruns translation using the saved disassembly. Older work folders need one translation after upgrading to record this information.

The build also records which decoder (the third_party/rpf9-explorer commit and the tools/rpf9dump sources) exported each archive's models and textures. When it changes, the assets stage removes that export and makes it again. Older work folders have no record, so their models and textures are exported once more after upgrading.

Stages run in order: check, shaders, assets, runtime, pipelines (creates every translated shader on your GPU driver and checks that it compiles, reports any it has to skip, and saves a pipeline cache to pipeline_cache.bin in --out; the runtime doesn't load that cache yet, so it doesn't speed up the first boot). The shader translation is the longest step: it runs on --jobs processes (half the CPU threads by default).

--wav is off by default because 16-bit PCM WAV is several times larger than Ogg Opus. It decodes the repackaged Ogg Opus streams to work\assets\audio\wav after the audio bank step; existing WAV files are skipped when a build resumes.

Vulkan diagnostics on Linux

With CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan development headers and loader installed:

cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build/linux
cmake --build runtime/build/linux --parallel
./runtime/build/linux/vk_pipeline_check /path/to/spirv

Pass the directory containing index.json and the translated SPIR-V files to vk_pipeline_check.

make_game.py runs on Linux too. The pipelines stage uses the vk_pipeline_check built above (runtime/build/linux, or runtime/build), and builds it there itself before any other work if it is missing.

Running the loader on Linux

The loader is a Windows program and runs under Wine or Proton; CI runs its tests under Wine on every change to runtime/ (the wine job of the Runtime workflow). On Linux the runtime stage cross-builds it into runtime/build/windows with clang-cl and lld-link (LLVM 19+, but not 22.1.7 or 22.1.8, see docs/testing.md; plain names, or all five LLVM tools with one version suffix such as clang-cl-21) against the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK that xwin lays out, in XWIN_DIR or ~/.local/share/xwin-sdk (docs/testing.md has the one-time xwin command). Without them the stage is left out of the default stages, and asking for it lists what is missing before any work starts. A Windows build made elsewhere works too, such as the runtime-windows artifact of that workflow's windows job, unzipped:

python3 -I make_game.py --runtime-build ~/Downloads/runtime-windows

Either way it copies gta6rt.exe and gta6rt_tls_host.dll into --out and writes gta6rt.sh next to them, which starts gta6rt.exe with wine, or with the Wine named by WINE (for Proton, its files/bin/wine). The same option skips the build on Windows.

How it works

Piece What it does Where
Version check Every package file's name, size and SHA-256 for each supported version game/, make_game.py
Shader pipeline Carves DXBC containers from shaders.rpf without its encrypted table of contents. Unpacks the XBCH → FSSM native RDNA2 program, disassembles it with LLVM (gfx1013) and translates it to SPIR-V tools/shader_carve.py, fssm_unpack.py, shader_disasm.py, rdna2spirv.py
Asset export Finds validated resources inside RPF9 archives and the loose .ttpf texture pools tools/rpf9dump (on rpf9-explorer's Core)
Runtime Maps the PE image, resolves imports to shims (GDK, XMem, d3d12_xs) runtime/
Research tools PE/RTTI inspection, raw carving, texture tiling probes, GPU test harnesses tools/, runtime/test/
Progress dashboard One offline page of what passes, what changed since it last passed and what blocks next, built from test results and the docs' own tables; nothing is written inside the repo tools/progress_dashboard.py

The translator's runtime contract (user SGPRs, push constants, memory model, bindless images, vertex fetch, system values) and all the format notes are in docs/design.md; the format, asset, runtime and validation notes are indexed in docs/README.md. The Xbox D3D12 plan is in docs/d3d12_vulkan.md. Audio bank formats and the export tools are in docs/audio.md; docs/related_projects.md records the prior art we may read and the licence limits on it.

Want to help?

The biggest open pieces:

  • Shader translator on hardware: compute, mesh and geometry now translate (see the translator contract in docs/design.md); still open are the vertex-shader input layout (v0 = VertexIndex is unverified if the console runs VS as NGG) and wave64 cross-half code in VS/PS/GS on 32-wide subgroups.
  • Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan: the d3d12_xs command list and descriptor heap model.
  • Model recovery: investigate the 71 unrecovered fragment candidates in levels.rpf.

See CONTRIBUTING.md. Never attach game files, extracted assets or generated shaders to issues or pull requests.

Credits

  • rpf9-explorer by breadbbbb: the RPF9 model, texture-pool and AWC decoders used by tools/rpf9dump (git submodule).
  • Mesa (MIT): GFX10 resource-descriptor layout (tools/gfx10_formats.json), and the ACO/RADV rules used as reference for 16-bit results and shader system registers.
  • libHttpClient (MIT) by Microsoft: the XTaskQueue/XAsync implementation in third_party/xtaskqueue, used by the offline xgameruntime shim.
  • LLVM: AMDGPU disassembler.
  • Logo: "Grand Theft Auto VI" icon by SlyDevil on SteamGridDB.
  • SPIRV-Tools: assembly and validation.

The runtime is Windows code: it cross-compiles with clang-cl and xwin, and its tests run under Wine or Proton (The Windows runtime on Linux, under Wine or Proton below). The game is meant to run the same way, under Wine or Proton with the D3D12 layer on native Vulkan (#217). macOS (Apple Silicon) The Python tools and the Vulkan test tools run natively, on MoltenVK (Homebrew) or KosmicKrisp. The runtime is Windows code and runs as on Linux, under Wine: CrossOver, arm64 with FEX or x86-64 under Rosetta (#1706, #1707, #1924; #3119 fixes the last loader tests there). Known gaps: no geometry stage and no VK_EXT_mesh_shader (those tests are skipped), 32-wide subgroups (wave64 shaders run emulated), and MoltenVK's float handling (PerVertexKHR, NaN compares, -0, the cost of NoContraction); docs/testing.md lists each (#2947). AMD RDNA1 (RX 5000) A supported target: close to the console's RDNA2, and its 64-wide subgroups run the wave64 shaders natively. RX 5700 XT results pass the GPU test suite (#146); on RADV, pixel shaders without fragment barycentrics have a known difference (Known problems in docs/testing.md) (#330). GPU results from every platform are collected in #166; how to run the tests is in docs/testing.md. How to build The port isn't downloaded ready-made. It's built on your PC from your own copy. The easy way: Install the prerequisites below. Download this project with its submodule: git clone --recursive https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out third_party/rpf9-explorer. The build fetches it if git is installed, and otherwise tells you what to do. Double-click Build.bat. It finds your copy of the game by itself: it looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents (also where Windows keeps them, such as in OneDrive), Games, your home folder and the top of every drive, two folders deep. It recognises the version from a few file sizes, without reading anything large. If you have more than one copy it asks which one, and if it finds none it asks you to paste the folder. Before starting it checks that everything below is installed and that there is enough free space, and it lists anything missing in one go. The result goes to Documents\Leonida. A stopped build continues where it left off. Your game folder is the one that holds MicrosoftGame.Config and the .rpf archives, as plain files. Prerequisites: Your own copy of the Xbox Series package, version 1.0.2.1. Windows 10/11 x64, with about 350 GB free for work files. They can go on another drive with --work. Python 3.12+ (tick "Add python.exe to PATH"). .NET 8 SDK. Vulkan SDK, for spirv-as / spirv-val. LLVM 21+ with the AMDGPU target for llvm-mc. The official Windows build has no AMDGPU target. On Windows, scripts\build_llvm_mc.ps1 builds a native llvm-mc.exe with it (no WSL; needs git and the Visual Studio C++ tools below) and sets LLVM_MC; it takes about 20-40 minutes. A faster way, if you use conda: conda install -c conda-forge llvm-tools (its Windows build includes the AMDGPU target; docs/testing.md used version 23.1.6), then set LLVM_MC to the full path of the llvm-mc.exe it installs (where llvm-mc shows it once the environment is active). Or install llvm-21 in WSL and set LLVM_MC to the whole command, LLVM_MC="wsl -d Ubuntu -e /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc" (see docs/design.md). On Linux, llvm-mc on PATH is enough. Visual Studio 2022 with Desktop development with C++ and the Windows SDK 10.0.26100 or newer, for the runtime stage (the runtime uses version 1.2 root signatures, which older SDKs don't declare). ffmpeg on PATH (optional: decodes the XMA2 streams, and required for --wav). Low disk space: the ~350 GB figure is for the full build. To run the port, --stages check,shaders,runtime needs about 30 GB; the assets stage (~300 GB) is only for the asset tools, and --wav adds several times the Ogg Opus size (the preflight prints this choice when the assets stage is what does not fit). --work and --out can sit on another drive. The runtime maps the package in place, so a read-only package drive needs gta6rt --overlay <writable folder>; --overlay is a gta6rt option, not a make_game.py one. Leave the .s files in work/shaders/dxbc/disasm in place: deleting them, along with the translated work/shaders/spirv/index.json, can leave the shaders stage looking finished with zero shaders. A disasm folder that is a symlink is refused when the stage has to clear it. From a terminal, with the same behaviour and more control: python -I make_game.py --find # list the copies found on this PC python -I make_game.py --pick # choose the game folder in a folder dialog python -I make_game.py --check # check your copy, build nothing python -I make_game.py --check --full-check # also compare SHA-256 of every file (slow) python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --out "D:\Games\Leonida" --work "E:\leonida-work" python -I make_game.py --stages shaders,assets # only some stages python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --wav # also decode Opus to PCM WAV (large) python -I make_game.py --wave64-emulate off # auto (default), on or off; see below --wave64-emulate decides whether wave64 compute and mesh shaders are translated to be exact on any subgroup size (see "Wave64 emulation" in docs/design.md). NVIDIA and Intel GPUs have 32-wide subgroups and need it. The default, auto, asks vulkaninfo (part of the Vulkan SDK) and turns emulation on if any GPU lacks 64-wide subgroups or its subgroup size is unknown. It also checks whether the runtime's GPU can run compute and mesh shaders 64-wide. With --mesh-compute, only compute subgroup support is needed. On AMD's Windows driver, auto uses native wave64 on RDNA1 and RDNA2 when the runtime's GPU supports it, even if another GPU is 32-wide or vulkaninfo is unavailable. That driver can crash on emulated LDS code (#857). For RDNA1 cards without mesh support, the decision uses the compute stage, which can run wave64 without native mesh support. The mode is saved next to the translated shaders, and changing it translates them again. auto can normally reuse previously emulated shaders. The AMD Windows workaround rebuilds those shaders in native mode. Use --wave64-emulate on to force emulation or --wave64-emulate off to force native wave64. Four fallback flags are forwarded to the translator the same way, saved next to the translated shaders, and changing them translates them again: --no-float-controls (drop SignedZeroInfNanPreserve, for devices whose pipeline check skips a shader without shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32; needs PR #664's translator flag), --bary-fallback (read raw barycentrics from an interpolated input, for devices without VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric), --texel-offset-fallback (fold image_sample*_o offsets into the coordinate, for devices without VK_KHR_maintenance8) and --mesh-compute (mesh shaders as compute, for devices without VK_EXT_mesh_shader). Each is documented in docs/design.md. The build records which llvm-mc command and version produced the disassembly. Changing either, or reusing a work folder that predates this record, reruns disassembly and translation while keeping the extracted shader inputs. The build records which translator sources produced the shaders. A change to those files reruns translation using the saved disassembly. Older work folders need one translation after upgrading to record this information. The build also records which decoder (the third_party/rpf9-explorer commit and the tools/rpf9dump sources) exported each archive's models and textures. When it changes, the assets stage removes that export and makes it again. Older work folders have no record, so their models and textures are exported once more after upgrading. Stages run in order: check, shaders, assets, runtime, pipelines (creates every translated shader on your GPU driver and checks that it compiles, reports any it has to skip, and saves a pipeline cache to pipeline_cache.bin in --out; the runtime doesn't load that cache yet, so it doesn't speed up the first boot). The shader translation is the longest step: it runs on --jobs processes (half the CPU threads by default). --wav is off by default because 16-bit PCM WAV is several times larger than Ogg Opus. It decodes the repackaged Ogg Opus streams to work\assets\audio\wav after the audio bank step; existing WAV files are skipped when a build resumes. Vulkan diagnostics on Linux With CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan development headers and loader installed: cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build/linux cmake --build runtime/build/linux --parallel ./runtime/build/linux/vk_pipeline_check /path/to/spirv Pass the directory containing index.json and the translated SPIR-V files to vk_pipeline_check. make_game.py runs on Linux too. The pipelines stage uses the vk_pipeline_check built above (runtime/build/linux, or runtime/build), and builds it there itself before any other work if it is missing. Running the loader on Linux The loader is a Windows program and runs under Wine or Proton; CI runs its tests under Wine on every change to runtime/ (the wine job of the Runtime workflow). On Linux the runtime stage cross-builds it into runtime/build/windows with clang-cl and lld-link (LLVM 19+, but not 22.1.7 or 22.1.8, see docs/testing.md; plain names, or all five LLVM tools with one version suffix such as clang-cl-21) against the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK that xwin lays out, in XWIN_DIR or ~/.local/share/xwin-sdk (docs/testing.md has the one-time xwin command). Without them the stage is left out of the default stages, and asking for it lists what is missing before any work starts. A Windows build made elsewhere works too, such as the runtime-windows artifact of that workflow's windows job, unzipped: python3 -I make_game.py --runtime-build ~/Downloads/runtime-windows Either way it copies gta6rt.exe and gta6rt_tls_host.dll into --out and writes gta6rt.sh next to them, which starts gta6rt.exe with wine, or with the Wine named by WINE (for Proton, its files/bin/wine). The same option skips the build on Windows. How it works Piece What it does Where Version check Every package file's name, size and SHA-256 for each supported version game/, make_game.py Shader pipeline Carves DXBC containers from shaders.rpf without its encrypted table of contents. Unpacks the XBCH → FSSM native RDNA2 program, disassembles it with LLVM (gfx1013) and translates it to SPIR-V tools/shader_carve.py, fssm_unpack.py, shader_disasm.py, rdna2spirv.py Asset export Finds validated resources inside RPF9 archives and the loose .ttpf texture pools tools/rpf9dump (on rpf9-explorer's Core) Runtime Maps the PE image, resolves imports to shims (GDK, XMem, d3d12_xs) runtime/ Research tools PE/RTTI inspection, raw carving, texture tiling probes, GPU test harnesses tools/, runtime/test/ Progress dashboard One offline page of what passes, what changed since it last passed and what blocks next, built from test results and the docs' own tables; nothing is written inside the repo tools/progress_dashboard.py The translator's runtime contract (user SGPRs, push constants, memory model, bindless images, vertex fetch, system values) and all the format notes are in docs/design.md; the format, asset, runtime and validation notes are indexed in docs/README.md. The Xbox D3D12 plan is in docs/d3d12_vulkan.md. Audio bank formats and the export tools are in docs/audio.md; docs/related_projects.md records the prior art we may read and the licence limits on it. Want to help? Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan: the d3d12_xs command list and descriptor heap model. Model recovery: investigate the 71 unrecovered fragment candidates in levels.rpf. See CONTRIBUTING.md. blocks.html_en: Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens on your PC, from your own copy of the game.

content_html_zh:
Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens on your PC, from your own copy of the game.

重要的

This repository does not contain the game, keys or an executable, and it does not explain how to get them. You need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files.

如何建造

The port isn't downloaded ready-made. It's built on your PC from your own copy.

The easy way:

  1. Install the prerequisites below.
  2. Download this project with its submodule: git clone --recursive https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out third_party/rpf9-explorer. The build fetches it if git is installed, and otherwise tells you what to do.
  3. Double-click Build.bat.

It finds your copy of the game by itself: it looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents (also where Windows keeps them, such as in OneDrive), Games, your home folder and the top of every drive, two folders deep. It recognises the version from a few file sizes, without reading anything large. If you have more than one copy it asks which one, and if it finds none it asks you to paste the folder. Before starting it checks that everything below is installed and that there is enough free space, and it lists anything missing in one go. The result goes to Documents\Leonida. A stopped build continues where it left off.

Your game folder is the one that holds MicrosoftGame.Config and the .rpf archives, as plain files.

先决条件：

  • Your own copy of the Xbox Series package, version 1.0.2.1.
  • Windows 10/11 x64, with about 350 GB free for work files. They can go on another drive with --work.
  • Python 3.12+ (tick "Add python.exe to PATH").
  • .NET 8 SDK.
  • Vulkan SDK, for spirv-as / spirv-val.
  • LLVM 21+ with the AMDGPU target for llvm-mc. The official Windows build has no AMDGPU target. On Windows, scripts\build_llvm_mc.ps1 builds a native llvm-mc.exe with it (no WSL; needs git and the Visual Studio C++ tools below) and sets LLVM_MC; it takes about 20-40 minutes. A faster way, if you use conda: conda install -c conda-forge llvm-tools (its Windows build includes the AMDGPU target; docs/testing.md used version 23.1.6), then set LLVM_MC to the full path of the llvm-mc.exe it installs (where llvm-mc shows it once the environment is active). Or install llvm-21 in WSL and set LLVM_MC to the whole command, LLVM_MC="wsl -d Ubuntu -e /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc" (see docs/design.md). On Linux, llvm-mc on PATH is enough.
  • Visual Studio 2022 with Desktop development with C++ and the Windows SDK 10.0.26100 or newer, for the runtime stage (the runtime uses version 1.2 root signatures, which older SDKs don't declare).
  • ffmpeg on PATH (optional: decodes the XMA2 streams, and required for --wav).

Low disk space: the ~350 GB figure is for the full build. To run the port, --stages check,shaders,runtime needs about 30 GB; the assets stage (~300 GB) is only for the asset tools, and --wav adds several times the Ogg Opus size (the preflight prints this choice when the assets stage is what does not fit). --work and --out can sit on another drive. The runtime maps the package in place, so a read-only package drive needs gta6rt --overlay <writable folder>; --overlay is a gta6rt option, not a make_game.py one. Leave the .s files in work/shaders/dxbc/disasm in place: deleting them, along with the translated work/shaders/spirv/index.json, can leave the shaders stage looking finished with zero shaders. A disasm folder that is a symlink is refused when the stage has to clear it.

From a terminal, with the same behaviour and more control:

python -I make_game.py --find                          # list the copies found on this PC
python -I make_game.py --pick                          # choose the game folder in a folder dialog
python -I make_game.py --check                         # check your copy, build nothing
python -I make_game.py --check --full-check            # also compare SHA-256 of every file (slow)
python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --out "D:\Games\Leonida" --work "E:\leonida-work"
python -I make_game.py --stages shaders,assets         # only some stages
python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --wav   # also decode Opus to PCM WAV (large)
python -I make_game.py --wave64-emulate off            # auto (default), on or off; see below

--wave64-emulate decides whether wave64 compute and mesh shaders are translated to be exact on any subgroup size (see "Wave64 emulation" in docs/design.md). NVIDIA and Intel GPUs have 32-wide subgroups and need it. The default, auto, asks vulkaninfo (part of the Vulkan SDK) and turns emulation on if any GPU lacks 64-wide subgroups or its subgroup size is unknown. It also checks whether the runtime's GPU can run compute and mesh shaders 64-wide. With --mesh-compute, only compute subgroup support is needed.

On AMD's Windows driver, auto uses native wave64 on RDNA1 and RDNA2 when the runtime's GPU supports it, even if another GPU is 32-wide or vulkaninfo is unavailable. That driver can crash on emulated LDS code (#857). For RDNA1 cards without mesh support, the decision uses the compute stage, which can run wave64 without native mesh support.

The mode is saved next to the translated shaders, and changing it translates them again. auto can normally reuse previously emulated shaders. The AMD Windows workaround rebuilds those shaders in native mode. Use --wave64-emulate on to force emulation or --wave64-emulate off to force native wave64.

Four fallback flags are forwarded to the translator the same way, saved next to the translated shaders, and changing them translates them again: --no-float-controls (drop SignedZeroInfNanPreserve, for devices whose pipeline check skips a shader without shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32; needs PR #664's translator flag), --bary-fallback (read raw barycentrics from an interpolated input, for devices without VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric), --texel-offset-fallback (fold image_sample*_o offsets into the coordinate, for devices without VK_KHR_maintenance8) and --mesh-compute (mesh shaders as compute, for devices without VK_EXT_mesh_shader). Each is documented in docs/design.md.

The build records which llvm-mc command and version produced the disassembly. Changing either, or reusing a work folder that predates this record, reruns disassembly and translation while keeping the extracted shader inputs.

The build records which translator sources produced the shaders. A change to those files reruns translation using the saved disassembly. Older work folders need one translation after upgrading to record this information.

The build also records which decoder (the third_party/rpf9-explorer commit and the tools/rpf9dump sources) exported each archive's models and textures. When it changes, the assets stage removes that export and makes it again. Older work folders have no record, so their models and textures are exported once more after upgrading.

Stages run in order: check, shaders, assets, runtime, pipelines (creates every translated shader on your GPU driver and checks that it compiles, reports any it has to skip, and saves a pipeline cache to pipeline_cache.bin in --out; the runtime doesn't load that cache yet, so it doesn't speed up the first boot). The shader translation is the longest step: it runs on --jobs processes (half the CPU threads by default).

--wav is off by default because 16-bit PCM WAV is several times larger than Ogg Opus. It decodes the repackaged Ogg Opus streams to work\assets\audio\wav after the audio bank step; existing WAV files are skipped when a build resumes.

Vulkan diagnostics on Linux

With CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan development headers and loader installed:

cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build/linux
cmake --build runtime/build/linux --parallel
./runtime/build/linux/vk_pipeline_check /path/to/spirv

Pass the directory containing index.json and the translated SPIR-V files to vk_pipeline_check.

make_game.py runs on Linux too. The pipelines stage uses the vk_pipeline_check built above (runtime/build/linux, or runtime/build), and builds it there itself before any other work if it is missing.

Running the loader on Linux

The loader is a Windows program and runs under Wine or Proton; CI runs its tests under Wine on every change to runtime/ (the wine job of the Runtime workflow). On Linux the runtime stage cross-builds it into runtime/build/windows with clang-cl and lld-link (LLVM 19+, but not 22.1.7 or 22.1.8, see docs/testing.md; plain names, or all five LLVM tools with one version suffix such as clang-cl-21) against the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK that xwin lays out, in XWIN_DIR or ~/.local/share/xwin-sdk (docs/testing.md has the one-time xwin command). Without them the stage is left out of the default stages, and asking for it lists what is missing before any work starts. A Windows build made elsewhere works too, such as the runtime-windows artifact of that workflow's windows job, unzipped:

python3 -I make_game.py --runtime-build ~/Downloads/runtime-windows

Either way it copies gta6rt.exe and gta6rt_tls_host.dll into --out and writes gta6rt.sh next to them, which starts gta6rt.exe with wine, or with the Wine named by WINE (for Proton, its files/bin/wine). The same option skips the build on Windows.
